jobs.description: Adjunct Faculty Job Openings Why You Should Teach at Maricopa Community Colleges Become an Adjunct Faculty Member At Maricopa Community Colleges, adjunct faculty make a lasting contribution to our students' success. Whether you're already a teacher or you're a professional looking to share your expertise, having the chance to influence students may make this the best part-time job you will ever have. Our adjunct faculty jobs offer schedule flexibility, competitive pay, and the chance to give back to your community. Completing this application process puts your information in a searchable "pool," to be accessed by hiring managers as needed. Before You Apply, Discover Which Colleges Offer Your Programs While all colleges offer general academic classes, each varies with which Career and Training Education (CTE) programs they offer. Our application process will ask you to identify which colleges should receive your application. To learn which colleges offer programs for your teaching qualifications, watch this quick video, then go to this webpage and click on Programs by Name. When you select your program, the menu in the upper left-hand corner will inform you which college(s) provide the right program. Alternatively, some of the colleges are listed in the program information. See Specific Discipline Qualifications Apply to Our Adjunct Pool Select a Field of Interest below to find your area of expertise, review position requirements, and submit your application, including your resume, cover letter, and supporting documents (PDF format required). In addition to submitting information and credentials to this adjunct pool, chairs and program managers can be contacted through email. Department and division contact information is available on each college website. Applied Technology In Applied Technology, you will teach students how to design, develop, or repair high-tech equipment and processes. Behavioral Science and Human Services Teach students how to work with community members to identify problems and create and implement solutions. Business, Entrepreneurialism, and Management Our Business, Entrepreneurialism, and Management pathway gives you the chance to teach the skills students need to be economic and social leaders. Computer and Information Technology Bring your real-world experience into the classroom to teach gaming, programming, tech support, web design, and more. Culture and Society Help your students tackle complex global issues in a wide range of programs, from communication and sociology to history, economics, and beyond. Education Use your love of teaching to help Education students reach their full potential as teachers, administrators, program planners, and more. First-Year Experience—Counseling Help students in any discipline plan and prepare for their careers by creating a foundation designed for success while they gain essential skills. Lead students through their First-Year Experience (FYE) classes. Training is provided. Counselors serve our students in all disciplines. Health Sciences In the Health Sciences Field of Interest, you will have the opportunity to share your clinical and field experience with our Health Sciences students. Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics Show students how they can creatively solve problems and explore new frontiers in STEM. Visual and Performing Arts Help students hone their craft in visual art, design, dance, music, fashion, film, or theatre.

jobs.title: Adjunct Faculty, Physics, Prescott Campus
jobs.description: Job DescriptionThe OpportunityThe Department of Physics & Astronomy at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University (Prescott, AZ) is searching for an adjunct physics instructor to teach undergraduate physics courses in person at ERAU's Prescott Campus. Courses taught in the department serve aviation, engineering, physics, and astronomy undergraduates. Instructors can teach 1-2 lecture courses or up to 4 labs in a semester. Preference will be given to candidates with prior teaching experience and hands-on physics laboratory skills.About usFor nearly 100 years, Embry-Riddle has been the world's leading aviation and aerospace university, educating more than 30,000 students across residential campuses in Daytona Beach, Florida, and Prescott, Arizona, as well as through a global network of Worldwide locations and online programs. With more than 165,000 alumni around the world, our impact reaches every corner of the aerospace, aviation, defense and technology industries.Today, our faculty, researchers and professional staff are advancing innovation across aviation, space, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, autonomous systems and next-generation engineering. Working alongside industry leaders, government agencies and innovators, they are solving real-world challenges and shaping the technologies that will define tomorrow.Whether you are an educator, researcher, administrator, technologist or industry professional, your work at Embry-Riddle will contribute to something bigger than a job. Join a community driven by discovery, purpose and excellence—and help shape the future of aerospace.QualificationsRequired Education and Qualifications:The qualified candidate must have a Masters Degree or PhD in physics, astronomy, or a closely related field.Application process/requirements:To submit your application for this opportunity, please visit the Embry-Riddle Career Site and search for requisition number R311500. Please attach all relevant materials to your application when you apply online. Complete submissions include:Cover letterFull CVContact information for at least three professional references (please note that references may be contacted as part of the interview/screening process)Current Embry-Riddle employees: Please apply directly through the ERAU Employee Hub Central application within Workday.Embry-Riddle is committed to fostering a workplace where all individuals are valued and respected. We strive to ensure that all faculty, staff, and students are treated fairly and provided equal opportunities for employment, advancement, compensation, training, and other benefits of employment. Embry-Riddle makes employment decisions — including hiring, promotions, compensation, and other terms of employment — based on individual merit, qualifications, and abilities. Embry Riddle is strongly opposed to discrimination and harassment, and such behavior is prohibited by university policy. Embry Riddle does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, disability, veteran status, predisposing genetic characteristics, age, religion, or pregnancy status, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law, in its employment, educational programs, admissions policies, financial aid, or other school-administered programs or activities. For further information, please visit our website. Embry-Riddle is not seeking assistance from staffing or recruitment agencies. All agencies are directed to contact eraujobs@erau.edu and should not reach out to hiring managers or staff.

jobs.title: Adjunct Faculty, Statistics
jobs.description: Job DescriptionBacked by the world’s largest and oldest university specializing in aviation and aerospace, Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, the Asia campus is looking for a passionate educator to support the course instruction to groom aviation leaders of tomorrow. The identified educator should demonstrate passion and extensive knowledge in the subject matter and be open to using engaging visuals, technologies and methods to facilitate knowledge transfer and interaction with undergraduate and graduate students. The adjunct faculty can look forward to teaching the following modules:Business Quantitative MethodsStatistics with Aviation ApplicationsBusiness StatisticsProbability and StatisticsDecision MathematicsThe above modules are non-exhaustive. QualificationsAt least a master’s or doctoral degree in Statistics Confident and comfortable to engage with large groupsProfessional experience in the aviation industry or teaching experience at a higher educational institution will be advantageousNote: This is an adjunct position where the faculty will be engaged for a nine-week term in a classroom setting. The faculty member will be required to teach up to six (6) hours per week in class. Each term consists of eight weeks of teaching and one week of examination and grading. The adjunct faculty must be available to teach during the day during weekdays and/or weekends.We apologize that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for interviews.
